Archie vs the chat app you already pay for.

You already have somewhere to ask an AI a question. The difference isn’t how clever the answer is: it’s who does the next part.

Archie is in testing. The waitlist hears the day it opens. See where it stands → Prices checked August 19, 2026; task capability checked September 14, 2026.

The short answer

Choose where the work runs.

Chat apps increasingly offer scheduled tasks and connected tools. Archie puts the agent, its files and its routines on your own computer. The choice depends on the accounts you need, where you want the work to run, and the controls you want.

A chat app suits you if

  • The work is thinking, drafting, and explaining
  • You want the answer now, while you’re sitting there
  • You’d rather nothing of yours was connected to anything
  • One flat monthly bill is easier to reason about than usage

An agent suits you if

  • The work repeats, and you keep forgetting to do it
  • It has to happen at seven in the morning, not when you remember
  • It needs your calendar and inbox to be any use at all
  • You want the reply drafted and waiting, not the advice about writing one

Where an agent wins

Five reasons to choose Archie.

Here is what Archie offers, with your computer on, awake and online.

Archie works while you are not asking

A brief before you are up, an inbox watched all day, a reminder that arrives when it should. None of it needs you to open anything.

Archie is signed into your life

Your calendar, your mail, your files, your to-do list and its own lists of people and projects, connected once and used every day, from your own computerSource 6.

Archie reaches you in the app you already have open

Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, or iMessage on a MacSource 4.

Archie asks before it acts

A calendar change is applied only after you approve it in a later message, and an email is a draft until you send it. Neither is a settingSource 5.

You choose the model, and you pay cost

Seven AI companies, on your own account, with a cap you setSource 4. The app is $30 a monthSource 3.

Where a chat app wins

Four things a chat app does better.

If any of these is what you came for, you already have the right tool.

Nothing to connect

A chat window with no access to your accounts cannot do anything wrong with them. That is a real security position, and it is the one Archie gives up in exchange for being useful while you are asleep.

A chat app works on your phone alone

No computer left on at home, no desktop app. Archie needs one awake; a chat app needs a signal.

One bill, no arithmetic

A flat subscription is easier to predict than pay-as-you-go usage, however carefully we model ours.

You can have a chat app in a minute

You can open one right now. Archie is in testing, and the waitlist hears the day it opens.

Worth saying

Most people end up wanting both.

Archie isn’t a replacement for the chat window, and it doesn’t try to be: it talks to the same AI companies, on your own account. Keep asking questions where you already ask them. Hand over the parts that repeat.
